chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:
I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about the hoopoe bird, its killing and its slaughtering, so he said: 'It is not harmed and it is not slaughtered; what a good bird it is.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing or slaughtering the hoopoe bird in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the specific status of the hoopoe (al-hudhud), ruling that it is neither to be harmed nor slaughtered for consumption, thereby distinguishing it from standard game animals. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of preserving specific creatures based on prophetic tradition, reflecting the bird's unique mention in the Quran for its role in Prophet Sulayman’s (AS) court.
